title: Recollecting the Buddha
hook: a deadline, a shortcut nobody would notice, and an old practice about who's in the room

segments.voice: Yesterday, why this practice: the unlovely is there to cool craving, never to aim hate at anyone. Now the manual turns from the body to three things to remember, starting with the Buddha.
screen: `TO COOL, NOT TO HATE.` → `NOW: THREE THINGS TO REMEMBER.`

segments.voice: Plenty of people act differently when a coach, a grandparent or a hero walks into the room. Shoulders go back. The phone goes away. A joke gets edited. So, yesterday's question: who would you want watching when nobody's watching? Buddhaghosa has an answer, and it comes with a practice: calling to mind the Buddha's qualities, buddhanussati. The words are old ones: iti pi so bhagava. Thus indeed is he, the Blessed One: worthy, fully awake, perfect in knowledge and conduct, and on down the list.
screen: `WHEN A HERO WALKS IN.` → `WHO'S WATCHING WHEN NOBODY IS?` → `ITI PI SO: THUS INDEED IS HE.`

segments.voice: Here's what the manual says happens to someone who keeps at it. He comes to feel as if he's living in the Teacher's presence. His body, Buddhaghosa says, becomes worthy of honor, like a shrine room. And the part that matters on an ordinary afternoon: when a chance to do wrong comes along, he feels conscience and shame as clearly as if he were standing face to face with the Teacher. Notice what that is, and what it isn't. It isn't a camera, or fear of being caught; there's no punishment in the passage. It's closer to the way a good mentor stays in your head long after the lesson. You hear the voice, and you'd rather be the person they saw in you. The manual adds an honest limit, too. Because the Buddha's qualities are so many and so deep, this recollection brings the mind to the edge of deep concentration, not all the way in. It's a practice for a steady, good-hearted day more than for a trance. So who would you want watching? Someone whose qualities you can name, one by one. That's why the old formula names them.
screen: `AS IF IN THE TEACHER'S PRESENCE.` · `CONSCIENCE, FACE TO FACE.` · `NOT A CAMERA: A MENTOR'S VOICE.` · `TO THE EDGE OF DEEP CALM.` · then, large: `THUS INDEED IS HE.`

segments.voice: If you'd like, say the opening line slowly, out loud or under your breath: iti pi so bhagava, thus indeed is he, the Blessed One. Then name a few qualities, one at a time: worthy, fully awake, perfect in knowledge and conduct. After each, pause and let that quality stand there, the way a mentor's face would.
Buddhanussati: recollecting the Buddha. Calling his qualities to mind, one by one, until it feels like being in his presence.
Your line: thus indeed is he. A face to keep in mind when nobody else is around. Day nineteen of forty.

howItsDone: Many Theravada Buddhists chant the recollection of the Buddha, iti pi so bhagava, in daily and temple chanting; as a meditation it is practiced by calling the qualities to mind one at a time, as Visuddhimagga 7 describes.

iti pi so.meaning: Pali: thus indeed is he, the opening of the recollection

bhagava.meaning: the Blessed One, a title of the Buddha

Buddhaghosa.meaning: the commentator who wrote the Path of Purification

sources.ref: Visuddhimagga 7 (recollection of the Buddha: the practitioner comes to feel as if living in the Master's presence; his body becomes worthy of veneration like a shrine room; when an opportunity for transgression arises, conscience and shame are as vivid as if face to face with the Master; because the special qualities are profound and many, the jhana reaches only access)
The recollection of the Buddha (iti pi so bhagava araham sammasambuddho vijjacaranasampanno …), as in AN 6.10 and SN 11.3

notes: Visuddhimagga 7 paraphrased: living as if in the Master's presence; the body like a shrine room; conscience and shame as if face to face with the Master; access concentration only, because the qualities are profound and many. Confirm.
Iti pi so was taught on day 1445 (the car-dashboard angle, SN 11.3); this day takes the Visuddhimagga's angle (conscience as if in the Teacher's presence) to avoid repeating it.
'Plenty of people act differently when a coach, a grandparent or a hero walks into the room' is an everyday observation, not a statistic.
